Example value: z_loss=1e-4. {"prompt": "def _gamma_difference_hrf(tr, oversampling=50, time_length=32., onset=0.,\n                          delay=6, undershoot=16., dispersion=1.,\n                          u_dispersion=1., ratio=0.167):\n    \"\"\" Compute an hrf as the difference of two gamma functions\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n\n    tr : float\n        scan repeat time, in seconds\n\n    oversampling : int, optional (default=16)\n        temporal oversampling factor\n\n    time_length : float, optional (default=32)\n        hrf kernel length, in seconds\n\n    onset: float\n        onset time of the hrf\n\n    delay: float, optional\n        delay parameter of the hrf (in s.)\n\n    undershoot: float, optional\n        undershoot parameter of the hrf (in s.)\n\n    dispersion : float, optional\n        dispersion parameter for the first gamma function\n\n    u_dispersion : float, optional\n        dispersion parameter for the second gamma function\n\n    ratio : float, optional\n        ratio of the two gamma components\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    hrf : array of shape(length / tr * oversampling, dtype=float)\n         hrf sampling on the oversampled time grid\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    time = np.arange(0, time_length, tr / oversampling)\n    hrf = (time - onset) ** dispersion * np.exp(-(time - onset) / delay)\n    hrf -= ratio * (time - onset) ** u_dispersion * np.exp(-(time - onset) / undershoot)\n    return hrf\n", "solution": "\n    from scipy.stats import gamma\n    dt = tr / oversampling\n    time_stamps = np.linspace(0, time_length, np.rint(float(time_length) / dt).astype(np.int))\n    time_stamps -= onset\n    hrf = gamma.pdf(time_stamps, delay / dispersion, dt / dispersion) -\\\n        ratio * gamma.pdf(\n        time_stamps, undershoot / u_dispersion, dt / u_dispersion)\n    hrf /= hrf.sum()\n    return hrf"}

Only lines\n    that are common in both sets are present in the dict, lines unique to one\n    of the sets are omitted.\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    return {lineno1: lines2.index(line) + 1 for lineno1, line in enumerate(lines1, 1) if line in lines2}\n", "solution": "\n    differ = difflib.Differ()\n    diff = differ.compare(lines1, lines2)\n\n    SAME = '  '\n    ADDED = '+ '\n    REMOVED = '- '\n    INFO = '? '\n\n    lineno_map = {}  # {lineno1: lineno2, ...}\n    lineno1_offset = 0\n    lineno2 = 1\n\n    for diffline in diff:\n        if diffline.startswith(INFO):\n            continue\n\n        if diffline.startswith(SAME):\n            lineno1 = lineno2 + lineno1_offset\n            lineno_map[lineno1] = lineno2\n\n        elif diffline.startswith(ADDED):\n            lineno1_offset -= 1\n\n        elif diffline.startswith(REMOVED):\n            lineno1_offset += 1\n            continue\n\n        lineno2 += 1\n\n    return lineno_map"}

{"prompt": "def _calc_waves(self, angular_freqs, profile):\n        \"\"\"Compute the wave numbers and amplitudes (up- and down-going).\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        angular_freqs: :class:`numpy.ndarray`\n            Angular frequency at which the waves are computed.\n\n        profile: :class:`~.base.site.Profile`\n            Site profile.\n        \"\"\"", "output": "\n    k = np.empty_like(angular_freqs)\n    amp_up = np.empty_like(angular_freqs)\n    amp_down = np.empty_like(angular_freqs)\n    for i, angular_freq in enumerate(angular_freqs):\n        k[i] = 2 * np.pi / profile.wavelength(angular_freq)\n        amp_up[i] = profile.amp_up(angular_freq)\n        amp_down[i] = profile.amp_down(angular_freq)\n\n    return k, amp_up, amp_down\n", "solution": "\n\n        # Compute the complex wave numbers of the system\n        wave_nums = np.empty((len(profile), len(angular_freqs)), np.complex)\n        for i, l in enumerate(profile):\n            wave_nums[i, :] = angular_freqs / l.comp_shear_vel\n\n        # Compute the waves. In the top surface layer, the up-going and\n        # down-going waves have an amplitude of 1 as they are completely\n        # reflected at the surface.\n        waves_a = np.ones_like(wave_nums, np.complex)\n        waves_b = np.ones_like(wave_nums, np.complex)\n        for i, l in enumerate(profile[:-1]):\n            # Complex impedance -- wave number can be zero which causes an\n            # error.\n            with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'):\n                cimped = ((wave_nums[i] * l.comp_shear_mod) /\n                          (wave_nums[i + 1] * profile[i + 1].comp_shear_mod))\n\n            # Complex term to simplify equations -- uses full layer height\n            cterm = 1j * wave_nums[i, :] * l.thickness\n\n            waves_a[i + 1, :] = (\n                0.5 * waves_a[i] *\n                (1 + cimped) * np.exp(cterm) + 0.5 * waves_b[i] *\n                (1 - cimped) * np.exp(-cterm))\n            waves_b[i + 1, :] = (\n                0.5 * waves_a[i] *\n                (1 - cimped) * np.exp(cterm) + 0.5 * waves_b[i] *\n                (1 + cimped) * np.exp(-cterm))\n\n            # Set wave amplitudes with zero frequency to 1\n            mask = ~np.isfinite(cimped)\n            waves_a[i + 1, mask] = 1.\n            waves_b[i + 1, mask] = 1.\n\n        # fixme: Better way to handle this?\n        # Set wave amplitudes to 1 at frequencies near 0\n        mask = np.isclose(angular_freqs, 0)\n        waves_a[-1, mask] = 1.\n        waves_b[-1, mask] = 1.\n\n        self._waves_a = waves_a\n        self._waves_b = waves_b\n        self._wave_nums = wave_nums"}

{"prompt": "def mean_first_passage_time(adjacency):\n    \"\"\"\n    Calculates mean first passage time of `adjacency`\n\n    The first passage time from i to j is the expected number of steps it takes\n    a random walker starting at node i to arrive for the first time at node j.\n    The mean first passage time is not a symmetric measure: `mfpt(i,j)` may be\n    different from `mfpt(j,i)`.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    adjacency : (N x N) array_like\n        Weighted/unweighted, direct/undirected connection weight/length array\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    MFPT : (N x N) ndarray\n        Pairwise mean first passage time array\n\n    References\n    ----------\n    .. [1] Goni, J., Avena-Koenigsberger, A., de Mendizabal, N. V., van den\n       Heuvel, M. P., Betzel, R. F., & Sporns, O. (2013). Exploring the\n       morphospace of communication efficiency in complex networks. PLoS One,\n       8(3), e58070.\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n    adjacency = np.array(adjacency)\n    N = adjacency.shape[0]\n    L = np.zeros((N, N))\n    for i in range(N):\n        for j in range(N):\n            if adjacency[i, j] > 0:\n                L[i, j] = 1 / adjacency[i, j]\n    D = np.diag(np.sum(L, axis=1))\n    Q = np.linalg.inv(D) @ L\n    I = np.eye(N)\n    MFPT = np.zeros((N, N))\n    for i in range(N):\n        for j in range(N):\n            if i!= j:\n                MFPT[i, j] = np.sum(np.linalg.inv(I - Q + np.diag(np.ones(N))) @ np.ones(N)) - 1\n\n    return MFPT\n", "solution": "\n\n    P = np.linalg.solve(np.diag(np.sum(adjacency, axis=1)), adjacency)\n\n    n = len(P)\n    D, V = np.linalg.eig(P.T)\n\n    aux = np.abs(D - 1)\n    index = np.where(aux == aux.min())[0]\n\n    if aux[index] > 10e-3:\n        raise ValueError(\"Cannot find eigenvalue of 1. Minimum eigenvalue \" +\n                         \"value is {0}. Tolerance was \".format(aux[index]+1) +\n                         \"set at 10e-3.\")\n\n    w = V[:, index].T\n    w = w / np.sum(w)\n\n    W = np.real(np.repeat(w, n, 0))\n    I = np.eye(n)\n\n    Z = np.linalg.inv(I - P + W)\n\n    mfpt = (np.repeat(np.atleast_2d(np.diag(Z)), n, 0) - Z) / W\n\n    return mfpt"}

{"prompt": "def hyperbolic_errors(hyp_axes, xvals,\n                      transformation=None, axes=None,\n                      means=None, correct_apparent_dip=True,\n                      reverse=False):\n    \"\"\"\n    Returns a function that can be used to create a view of the\n    hyperbolic error ellipse from a specific direction.\n\n    This creates a hyperbolic quadric and slices it to form a conic\n    on a 2d cartesian plane aligned with the requested direction.\n\n    A function is returned that takes x values (distance along nominal\n    line) and returns y values (width of error hyperbola)\n\n    kwargs:\n        transformation  rotation to apply to quadric prior to slicing\n                        (e.g. transformation into 'world' coordinates\n        axes            axes on which to slice the data\n    \"\"\"", "output": "\n\n    def view_hyperbola(xvals):\n        return yvals\n\n    return view_hyperbola\n", "solution": "\n    if means is None:\n        means = N.array([0,0])\n\n    arr = augment_tensor(N.diag(hyp_axes))\n\n    # Transform ellipsoid to dual hyperboloid\n    hyp = conic(arr).dual()\n\n    if len(hyp_axes) == 3:\n        # Three_dimensional case\n\n        if transformation is None:\n            transformation = N.identity(3)\n        if axes is None:\n            axes = N.array([[0,1,0],[0,0,1]])\n\n        hyp = hyp.transform(augment_tensor(transformation))\n\n        n_ = N.cross(axes[0],axes[1])\n\n        # Create a plane containing the two axes specified\n        # in the function call\n        p = plane(n_) # no offset (goes through origin)\n        h1 = hyp.slice(p, axes=axes)[0]\n    else:\n        # We have a 2d geometry\n        h1 = hyp\n\n    # Major axes of the conic sliced in the requested viewing\n    # geometry\n    A = N.sqrt(h1.semiaxes())\n\n    yvals = A[1]*N.cosh(N.arcsinh(xvals/A[0]))\n\n    vals = N.array([xvals,yvals]).transpose()\n    nom = N.array([xvals,N.zeros(xvals.shape)]).transpose()\n\n    # Rotate the whole result if the PCA axes aren't aligned to the\n    # major axes of the view coordinate system\n    ax1 = apparent_dip_correction(axes)\n\n    # This is a dirty hack to flip things left to right\n    if reverse:\n        ax1 = ax1.T\n    # Top\n    t = dot(vals,ax1).T+means[:,N.newaxis]\n    # Btm\n    vals[:,-1] *= -1\n    b = dot(vals,ax1).T+means[:,N.newaxis]\n\n    nom = dot(nom,ax1).T+means[:,N.newaxis]\n    return nom, b, t[:,::-1]"}

{"prompt": "def lmedian (inlist,numbins=1000):\n    \"\"\"\nReturns the computed median value of a list of numbers, given the\nnumber of bins to use for the histogram (more bins brings the computed value\ncloser to the median score, default number of bins = 1000).
